acceptanceCriteria: Root cause of the absent .git/taskman.checkpoint.json on the real store is cited by file:line.

After any successful native write, a later read (queue status, ticket list, ticket search) uses a verified checkpoint and does not run the full receipt audit; a stale or forged checkpoint still falls back to the full audit.
A regression test fails on the pre-fix base and passes after.
Before/after timings of queue status and ticket list on a scratch copy of the real store are retained in the build log.
body: Observed 2026-10-09 by the Tasks read facets lane (corvint-tasks from origin/main 02e84575): on /Users/russelllewis/projects/corvint the file .git/taskman.checkpoint.json is absent although the store has had many native writes today. Only writers create it (retainCheckpoint), so every queue status and ticket list read runs the full receipt audit, about 2-3 s each. Expected: a verified checkpoint lets count and search reads return in well under 0.5 s. Actual: 2-3 s per read. The owner asked that counts such as tickets left to 1.0 and every other search be effectively instant. Suspected defect until the root cause is confirmed.

completion.reason: Merged via beamfall/corvint#708 (1120e565). Root cause cited in docs/build-log/2026-10-09-tasks-read-facets.md: the installed runtime predated checkpoint retention; no in-tree writer defect, so no code fix and the regression criterion is met by TestCALV0060_WritersRetainACheckpointReadsResumeFromIt. After build 402, reads report CHECKPOINT_PLUS_TAIL, 0.28 s vs about 2.1 s. Live qualification NOT_RUN.

title: corvint-tasks reads run the full receipt audit because the real store has no checkpoint (2-3 s per queue status/ticket list)
